solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: City where lives must go on as normal

indicators.note: IS must go on after the other piece, so it is placed second

parts.note: par is the normal or standard level, as in 'on a par'
'lives' in the sense 'exists' gives IS, as in 'he is'

explanation.surface: A city where people insist life carries on as usual despite everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Union of College with High that's illegal here

definitions.text: Union of College with High that's illegal here

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a kind of college
high meat, like game kept a long time, is gamy

explanation.surface: A merger of a college and a high school that breaks the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The merger of two institutions is really a marriage to several spouses, which is illegal in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Polygamy is marriage to more than one spouse at once, a union outlawed in the UK.

clue.text: Filth of river: one lifted dog out of water

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: in a down answer lifted means the dog word is read upwards

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador, a breed of dog
something out of water is dry

explanation.surface: Muck from a river as a dog is hauled up onto the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is coarse, vulgar humour, filth in the sense of smut.

clue.text: One chap's rival wins fresh conflict

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A man's competitor triumphs in a renewed fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939 was a major armed conflict.

clue.text: Pad cushioned and strapped?

parts.note: a pad is slang for a home, a flat
to cushion a fall is to break it, so cushioned means broke

explanation.surface: A padded item that is both cushioned and fitted with straps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strapped' looks like part of the padding picture, but it is the definition: strapped for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped is slang for short of money, and flat broke means having no money at all.

clue.text: Toss drink and lose it

definitions.meaning: to ... a coin is to toss it
a mixed drink, often with beaten egg
to lose one's temper or composure

explanation.surface: Throw your drink and lose your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip has three senses: throw with a flick, a mixed drink, and losing control.

clue.text: Take out girl — one I left consumed with passion

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the second I and left are swallowed up inside the passion word

parts.note: hate is a strong passion

explanation.surface: Taking a girl out, with a lover left burning with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take out' suggests a date, but it means kill or destroy.
explanation.definitionFit: To take out is slang for to kill or destroy, which is to annihilate.

clue.text: Store stuck with live bingo

parts.note: things bonded together are stuck
'we live' means 'we are', giving ARE
House! is the cry of a winner at bingo or housey-housey

explanation.surface: A shop that sticks with live bingo nights.
explanation.walkthrough: A bingo winner in Britain may shout 'House!' instead of 'Bingo!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonded warehouse is a store where dutiable goods are kept until tax is paid.

clue.text: I must keep small boy towing the line

indicators.note: the number word must keep, that is hold inside it, the boy's name

parts.note: I as a number is one
Sid is a short form of the boy's name Sidney

explanation.surface: I have to look after a little lad who is towing a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towing' plays on the phrase 'toeing the line', keeping to the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Being onside means in agreement and supportive, toeing the line; 'towing' is a deliberate pun.

clue.text: Standard, partially declining, is never going up

indicators.note: in a down answer going up means the letters are read upwards
only part of these words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A standard that is only partly falling and never rising.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a flag, and a standard is also a flag.

clue.text: Lender almost smiling: it's on the house!

indicators.note: in an across answer the trimmed smiling word sits on, that is after, the house

parts.note: Libra is one of the twelve houses (signs) of the zodiac

indicators.note: almost the whole word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: riant is a literary word for smiling or cheerful

explanation.surface: A cheerful moneylender offers a loan free, as if the bar were standing drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the house' suggests a free drink, but the house is the zodiac house Libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian lends books to borrowers, so is a lender in a crossword sense.

clue.text: Narrow margin's inches

definitions.meaning: a nose is a narrow winning margin in a horse race; read as a plural
to inch forward is to nose forward, edging slowly ahead

explanation.surface: A tiny winning margin measured in inches.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by a nose means a tiny margin, and nosing ahead is creeping forward inch by inch.

clue.text: Private collection primarily including the works of such as Balzac

indicators.note: the soldier's letters include, that is contain, the everything word

parts.note: a private soldier is a GI in American usage
'the works' means everything, all

indicators.note: primarily means taking only the first letter of the word collection

explanation.surface: A private art collection that mainly includes the works of Balzac and his like.
explanation.definitionFit: Balzac was a French novelist, and Gallic means French.

clue.text: One put on trial, eg, hoped thus finally to reform

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the word thus is used
to reform is to re-form, so the letters are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: A defendant hopes his trial will finally reform him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' makes HEEPDOG from EG HOPED. The trial is not in court: sheepdog trials are competitions herding sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepdogs compete in sheepdog trials, so a sheepdog is one put on trial.

clue.text: Work with football team keeping one quiet long into the night?

indicators.note: the club's letters keep, that is hold within, one and quiet

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United football club
the Roman numeral I is one
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
something going on long into the night is late

explanation.surface: A footballer working with the team while keeping quiet into the small hours.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something is to handle or manoeuvre it skilfully, which is to manipulate it.

clue.text: Sweets and chocolate bar that has approval from the sovereign?

parts.note: a Mars is a well-known chocolate bar
HM is His or Her Majesty, the sovereign
one who allows something approves of it

explanation.surface: Sweets and a chocolate bar granted a royal warrant by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshmallows are soft spongy confections, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Refer to eccentric golfer's top: an impressive jumper!

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are jumbled
the top of a down word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pointing to a golfer's wild sweater as a remarkable jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges REFER TO into TREEFRO. 'jumper' suggests a sweater, but it is a leaping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tree frogs are amphibians able to make remarkable leaps, so they are impressive jumpers.

clue.text: One present of a shirt for nurse to wear

indicators.note: the nurse word goes into the shirt as if wearing it

parts.note: a tee is a T-shirt
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A gift of a shirt for a nurse to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift but means being there.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone who is present at an event.

clue.text: Get wrong Times reprint for distribution

indicators.note: letters handed out for distribution are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper reprint sent out for distribution that gets things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinterpret something is to understand it wrongly, to get it wrong.

clue.text: State of fruit topping one put together

parts.note: a haw is the red fruit of the hawthorn
A1 means first-rate or topping, written AI
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A fruit dessert topping assembled from parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii is the fiftieth state of the USA.

clue.text: Deer and young bear perhaps raised in cave

indicators.note: in a down answer raised means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer
a cub is a young bear, or young fox or lion

explanation.surface: A deer and a bear cub brought up in a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in cave in.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to collapse under pressure, and so is to buckle.

clue.text: Al Capone's version?

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol of the metal; the American gangster Capone would use the American spelling of its name

explanation.surface: The gangster's own account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans spell the metal without the British extra I.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags that Al is the symbol for the metal, and Capone's version is the United States spelling.

clue.text: Take things easy at first — in time place very busy

indicators.note: the first letter of easy goes in the other letters

parts.note: a hive is a very busy place, a hive of activity

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of easy is used

explanation.surface: Relax at first, then you'll find yourself somewhere hectic.
explanation.definitionFit: To thieve is to steal, that is to take things belonging to others.

clue.text: Historic payment that is put on the books

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: sc., scilicet, is Latin for namely or that is
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An old payment that is entered in the accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot was a historic tax or levy, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Request team playing hands to one side

parts.note: to request is to ask
in bridge East and West form a partnership playing hands against North and South

explanation.surface: Asking a card team to deal their hands off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Askew means crooked, set at an angle or off to one side.

clue.text: Equipped with answer to expose Marxist on City Council

indicators.note: in an across answer the exposing and Marxist pieces go on, after, the council

parts.note: CC abbreviates City Council or County Council
to out someone is to expose them
red is the traditional label for a communist or Marxist

explanation.surface: Armed with a response to unmask a communist on the local council.
explanation.definitionFit: Accoutred means dressed or kitted out with the necessary gear, that is equipped.

clue.text: I close venue for undesirables urgently

parts.note: close in the sense of nearby means near
a nest is a haunt of villains, as in a nest of thieves

explanation.surface: Someone urgently shutting down a den of undesirables.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in earnest means seriously and with determination, so urgently fits loosely as a manner adverb.

clue.text: For which we say golfer should be dismissed, oddly!

definitions.text: For which we say golfer should be dismissed, oddly!

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of these words are dismissed, leaving the even-placed ones

explanation.surface: A puzzling exclamation about a golfer who ought to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike out the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of WE SAY GOLFER and what remains spells the answer. An eagle, two under par, is a score for which golfers are congratulated, not dismissed: hence 'oddly!'
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a golf score two strokes under par for a hole, something a golfer cheers.
